summary: Implemented four orchestrator API route handlers in gui/api.ts: handleOrchestratorStart (validates body.planPath + forwards dryRun), handleGetOrchestratorQueue, handleOrchestratorKill, handleOrchestratorDismiss.

Wired all four endpoints in gui/server.ts: GET /api/orchestrator/queue added to matchRoute(); POST /api/orchestrator/start|kill/:id|dismiss/:id added as special-case blocks in handleRequest() with correct body parsing and 204 No Content for dismiss.
Added 23 unit tests in tests/gui/api-orchestrator.test.ts covering all 6 acceptance criteria. All 639 GUI tests pass with no regressions.

comments.note: server.ts apiErrorToStatus() in gui/server.ts has no 'CONFLICT' case, so api.ts conflict() errors fall through to 500 status. Pre-existing issue — not introduced by WP-008. A CONFLICT → 409 mapping entry should be added to apiErrorToStatus().

handleOrchestratorStart does not thread logsDir through to startOrchestrator() — that function derives its own logs directory from workspaceRoot. The logsDir parameter was removed from the handler signature for cleanliness. No impact since startOrchestrator() uses the canonical path.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified via code inspection and test execution.

23 new unit tests in api-orchestrator.test.ts cover all AC: planPath validation (missing, number, null, non-object body), dryRun forwarding (true/false/default), queue enrichment, kill result shape, dismiss void resolution, and assertSafeQueueId guard.
Full GUI regression suite: 639 tests / 22 files — all pass.

server.ts routing verified: POST /api/orchestrator/start parses JSON body and dispatches WORKSPACE_ROOT; GET /api/orchestrator/queue via matchRoute(); kill/:id and dismiss/:id as special-case blocks with correct 200/204 responses.
decodeURIComponent() called before assertSafeQueueId — URL-encoded path separators (%2F) are decoded first, then caught by the guard. Security posture intact.

comments.note: assertSafeQueueId does not guard against a single '.' ID. Not a real-world concern (no queue entry would have ID '.'), but worth noting. Pre-existing design choice.
No body size limit on POST /api/orchestrator/start — very large JSON bodies would be read in full. Pre-existing pattern across all POST handlers in server.ts; not introduced by WP-008.

summary: Reviewed 4 files: gui/api.ts (new handlers + assertSafeQueueId), gui/server.ts (routing blocks), gui/orchestrator-manager.ts (startOrchestrator, killQueueEntry, dismissQueueEntry), src/utils/ledger-root.ts (WORKSPACE_ROOT). All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium (pre-existing, not introduced by WP-008). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01/A03 — assertSafeQueueId (api.ts:127): guard correctly checks for empty string, '/', and '..'. decodeURIComponent() is called in server.ts BEFORE assertSafeQueueId, so %2F-encoded slashes are decoded first then caught. ID is only used for string equality (findIndex) — not to build a file path — so Windows backslash is not a traversal vector here. Guard is sound.

A01 — startOrchestrator (orchestrator-manager.ts): planPath from HTTP body passes checkPathPrefix() (resolve()-based containment check) before any stat() call, eliminating TOCTOU path traversal risk. plan-basename and plan-file checks add further constraints. spawn() uses array arguments (no shell), preventing shell injection (A03). No findings.

A01 — removeLockFile (orchestrator-manager.ts): uses entry.planPath from the queue file (Python-written, not from the HTTP request body). Not directly controllable via the API. Risk is bounded to local file system access, acceptable for a localhost dev tool.

A04 — readBody() in server.ts (line 164) accumulates all chunks without a size cap. A crafted large POST body to /api/orchestrator/start (or any POST handler) would be read fully into memory before rejection. Pre-existing pattern across all POST handlers — not introduced by WP-008. Recommended fix: add a MAX_BODY_BYTES constant (~1 MB) and reject with 413 when exceeded. Low impact for a localhost tool; medium severity as a design debt item.

A05 — Security headers (server.ts:107): X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, and Content-Security-Policy are applied to all responses. CORS is restricted to http://localhost:{port}. Error responses return structured JSON without stack traces. Configuration is well-hardened.
A02/A06 — No new npm dependencies introduced by WP-008. No cryptographic operations. No sensitive data stored or transmitted. No CVE exposure from new code.

WORKSPACE_ROOT derivation (ledger-root.ts): tsconfig.json sets rootDir: './src' and outDir: './dist', so compiled output is dist/utils/ledger-root.js. join(__dirname, '..', '..') correctly resolves to mcp-server/ in both dev (tsx, runs .ts from src/utils/) and production (dist/utils/). workspaceRoot = join(serverDir, '..') correctly points to ai-insights/ workspace root in both environments. QA concern resolved — no security issue.
No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified.

summary: Reviewed 4 files: gui/api.ts (handlers + assertSafeQueueId), gui/server.ts (routing blocks), src/utils/ledger-root.ts (WORKSPACE_ROOT export), tests/gui/api-orchestrator.test.ts (23 tests). All 6 acceptance criteria met. Code is clean, follows established patterns, and is well-tested. PASS — no blocking issues, no fix-forward changes required.

comments.note: handleOrchestratorStart body check (api.ts:1538-1540) does not explicitly guard against array inputs — typeof [] === 'object' && [] !== null passes the first guard, so an array body falls through to the planPath check and produces a slightly misleading error message ('body.planPath is required' rather than 'Request body must be a JSON object'). Error code is still VALIDATION_ERROR (correct). Non-blocking: JSON.parse of a real API request body won't produce a bare array for this endpoint in practice. Fix: add `|| Array.isArray(body)` to the first condition if strict message accuracy is desired.

assertSafeQueueId (api.ts:127) is structurally identical to assertSafeWpId — same three guards, different error message. Both are intentionally kept separate because the error messages reference the specific parameter type ('queue entry ID' vs 'work-package ID'), which is the right trade-off for debuggability. No change needed.

[documentation-forward] apiErrorToStatus() in gui/server.ts is missing a CONFLICT → 409 case — conflict() errors currently fall through to 500. Pre-existing gap, not introduced by WP-008. api-surface.md should document the current mapping table and note the CONFLICT gap as a known limitation so future contributors know to add the missing case before using conflict() in any new handler.

No observations on WORKSPACE_ROOT export from ledger-root.ts — placement alongside ORCHESTRATOR_LOGS_DIR is correct and consistent. orchestratorLogsDir is correctly initialised from ORCHESTRATOR_LOGS_DIR at server startup (server.ts:746) and threaded through handleRequest to kill/dismiss handlers. Routing placement is sound: GET /api/orchestrator/queue in matchRoute(), POST start/kill/:id/dismiss/:id as special-case blocks before matchRoute() — appropriate because the body-parsing and path-param extraction blocks don't fit matchRoute's return-handler pattern.

notes: WP-008 introduces four new orchestrator route handlers and their HTTP routes.
POST /api/orchestrator/start — body: { planPath: string, dryRun?: boolean }; returns StartResult (checks[], started, pid?).
GET /api/orchestrator/queue — returns QueueEntry[] with effectiveStatus and progress fields.
POST /api/orchestrator/kill/:id — returns { killed: boolean }; 400 NOT_FOUND for invalid IDs.
POST /api/orchestrator/dismiss/:id — returns 204 No Content on success; 404 NOT_FOUND for invalid IDs.
WORKSPACE_ROOT is now exported from src/utils/ledger-root.ts and used in server.ts to resolve the workspace root for startOrchestrator().
